title: LensDefinition
description: The grammar for a lens definition: a declarative pattern the runtime evaluator turns into a matched subgraph (data lens) or type-graph slice (schema lens). A lens names slots (node bindings) and edges (relationship bindings); a slot is free (bound to a `type`) or pinned (bound to a specific instance via `ref`). Groupings are data lenses with a pinned anchor plus a `scope`. Backward-compatible with the original `{ name, nodes, edges, sentence }` shape — every field beyond `name`/`nodes` is optional and `target` defaults to `data`.

target.description: Whether the lens reads/returns the type graph (schema) or the instance graph (data). Defaults to data.

nodes.description: Slot bindings. Each binds a name to a node type; an optional `ref` pins it to a specific instance (data lenses only).

slot.description: The slot name referenced by edges and scopes.

type.description: The node type bound to this slot.

ref.description: Pins the slot to a specific instance (concrete id) or a predicate (select).

edges.description: Free edge bindings: links of relationship type `via` between the `from` and `to` slots.

scope.description: How a grouping expands from a pinned anchor slot.

from.description: The name of a pinned slot this scope expands from.

depth.description: A fixed hop count, or 'transitive' for unbounded (cycle-safe) expansion.
